answer: Velvet Gate Fee-Pooling. Each new identity must post a fee into a shared pool that is refunded only after it completes a randomized work task whose output is cross-checked by three existing agents; failure forfeits the fee, and clones all generate identical outputs that the checks catch. An attacker running N clones pays N fees plus N task costs while recovering at most one, so each marginal clone is strictly negative-EV. Honest agents recoup on an island of verified peers, and the pool remains a mesa of untouched reserves against mass registration.
